implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's own command independently on a rig I rebuilt from scratch in this pod: `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait` against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector. Both proofs hold. Its first proof: the round-1 red row 'a comment on words that read twice keeps the reading its author selected' passes (1.3m), the comment landing on the second reading after the tab was offline past the sweep's TTL. Its second: 'an ask whose selected text another writer deleted is not called a comment' passes (4.7s). failures.criterion: 2. The comment is created and anchored to the selected text (plan acceptance 2), and the rule the INFRA-512 architect's decision of 2026-10-30T09:49:42Z rests on: a record on a passage the reader never selected is worse than a refusal, because no refusal ever tells them about it
failures.evidence: A re-anchor takes the wrong reading when the reader's block GAINS a reading of the same words. Red test: packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts, 'a comment keeps its own reading when another writer adds an earlier one' (commit 299187eaaa24). Paragraph 'Alpha the lazy dog. Beta the lazy dog.'; the reader selects the second reading of 'the lazy dog' (character 25); another writer rewrites the paragraph to 'Zero the lazy dog. Alpha the lazy dog. Beta the lazy dog.', which takes the provisional mark and puts a reading in FRONT of the reader's. Run `cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait`: the row fails with 'offset 25 received, 44 expected' - the comment was created, not orphaned, over 'Alpha the lazy dog', while the reader's own words sit untouched at character 44. Nothing tells the reader. Mechanism, read in packages/proof-editor/src/record-mark-retype.ts remarkRange: the remembered placement is {blockId, reading: 1}; readingsInBlock is asked for at most placement.reading+1 readings and the range taken is readings[min(reading, length-1)], so a block that gained readings is the one case the index cannot survive - the block's own unit test beside it ('falls to the block's last reading where it now holds fewer') covers only the block that lost them. The row accepts either correct answer: the reader's own reading, or a refusal with the draft kept; only a different passage fails it. The INFRA-512 architect has decided this is a defect and amended the design on the pull request: the re-anchor becomes a text-quote selector (the selected words with a short prefix and suffix, attaching only where words and context both match once), which also changes the deleted-block fallback below.

environment: My pod and its volume were both replaced during this round, so the e2e rig built in round 1 was gone with them. I rebuilt it as one idempotent script on the issue volume, /legion/scratch/harness/setup.sh with env.sh beside it, following docs/solutions/testing/a-browser-harness-in-an-issue-pod-lives-on-the-issue-volume-INFRA-43.md: a rootless PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.0-1 unpacked from Debian packages (apt in this image carries no source for the server deb, so it is fetched from the Debian pool by name; 0.8.0-1 is the only postgresql-17 build of pgvector in the pool) and Playwright's Chromium under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH on the same volume. `bun install` and a build of @legion/contracts (`cd packages/contracts && bun run build`) are needed first, or every e2e row dies importing @legion/contracts/dist. A later role can re-run that one script. I restored bun.lock, which `bun install` had modified, before committing.
